content_html:
Every June 24, Cusco, the ancient capital of the Inca Empire, is transformed into a setting full of mysticism, history and tradition. The Inti Raymi 2025, or Sun Festival, shone brightly again, gathering thousands of people to pay tribute to Inti, the sun god.

What is Inti Raymi?

The Inti Raymi is a Inca ancestral celebration that marks the winter solstice in the southern hemisphere. For the Incas, it was the beginning of a new agricultural and spiritual year. Today, this festival revives with a impressive staging in three emblematic places in Cusco:

  • Qorikancha (Temple of the Sun)
  • Plaza de Armas of Cusco
  • Sacsayhuamán

Inti Raymi 2025: Color, history and living culture

This year, the Inti Raymi dazzled with typical costumes, ancestral music, ceremonial dances and a recreation of the Inca in its maximum splendor. More than 600 actors participated in the performance, captivating both locals and tourists from around the world.

A tourist and spiritual experience

More than a party, Inti Raymi is a connection with the Andean worldview. Participating in this celebration allows you to learn about the Inca legacy up close and live a unique experience in the Andes.
